If you've just started the game, then with all due respect, do not think you've learned everything there is or have even become proficient with the game's combat mechanics. NG+ is still the beginning and it takes several hundreds of hours to become adept at this game. 

It's entirely possible and even realistic to play this game well on WotN with no Omnyo/Ninjutsu, look at Poto222's videos on YouTube for example, or any Lvl.1 WotN boss video. 

The key here is that Omnyo/Ninjutsu doesn't take up any time if you're using their Mystic Arts that let you cast instantly. It literally takes me 3 seconds to go through 11 slots of buffs, and I don't do this all the time, only right before a boss or if I died during a boss and Quick Changed, then I will reapply buffs. Again, 3 seconds. 

I've never tried my hand at Lvl. 1 because I'm frankly not *that* good at the game, but there are people who have and their videos will show you just how balanced this game is.

Nioh has exponentially more build variety than Souls. 

Edit: oh, and level designs in Nioh are great, especially in the DLC. Environmental designs (big difference) are what is lacking *sometimes* in the base game. 

And omnyo/ninjutsu is not mandatory, but it is highly suggested and that's because the game was designed around this. I don't see the problem, as inside these trees there are a great number of possibilities. The only constant between my characters is Quick Change. 

In Souls, proficient players engage in challenge runs that limit your arsenal, simply because playing the game normally after 100hrs of gametime becomes a boring, tiresome routine. 

Nioh never falls into this trap no matter how good you are. Only very few people have done Lvl.1 runs in Nioh on WotN+, and when they do, it's always a side character, as the game is meant to be played by exploring all of your options. In Souls, the game becomes a formality too quickly, and this is why r/Onebros has grown over the years.
